name: Africa Restaurant
desc: Eritrian

name: Piccolo Arancio
desc: Small restaurant with a lot of Italian guests (but they are tourists, not Romans...) and moderate prices.

name: Il Gelato di San Crispino
desc: Considered one of the best ice creams in Rome. Check out the meringue ice creams and the fruit sorbets according to the season.

name: Gelato g Italiano
desc: An excellent ice-cream, one minute walk from Fontana di Trevi

name: Dagnino Tea Room, Galleria
desc: If you haven't tried a "Cannolo" or a "Cassatina" then get one here, they are simply great. Don't sit at the tables (it's pretty expensive) just take them away. Good pastries too.

name: Druid’s Rock Pub
desc: The sister pub of the Druid’s Den.

name: Palazzo del Freddo
desc: Ice cream: not as marvellous as Giolitti or San Crispino but still worth trying. Prices are reasonable, quality good. Old ice cream making equipment on display.

name: Ristorante Baia Chia
desc: Good value Sardinian fish restaurant. Seafood antipasto, three pasta dishes, grilled fish and dessert for around €40. Don't try to order, just let them bring it to your table. Excellent Sardinian wines extra.

name: Panella L’Arte del Pane
desc: Very upmarket (with matching prices) baker. Great window displays but you may find the taste doesn't match the appearance.

name: Aquila Nera, Ristorante Pizzeria
price: €25-35 for dinner including wine and bot

name: La Cuccuma
desc: Pizza by the slice, meatballs, and lasagna served in a simple restaurant with traditional furnishings.

name: La Forchetta d´Oro
addr: Via di S. Martino Ai Monti, 40

name: La Prezzemolina
desc: Pizzeria

name: Trattoria Pizzeria Luzzi
addr: Via di S. Giovanni in Laterano, 88

name: Gelateria S.M. Maggiore
desc: Particularly delicious gelato, including some special flavors, such as ricotta with figs and chocolate with oranges.

name: Pizza Forum
desc: The best lunch spot near the Colosseum, if you like pizza. You will get huge, delicious woodfire oven pizzas starting at about €5 each.

name: Est! Est! Est!!!

name: Cafè Cafè

name: Enoteca Cavour
desc: Great wine bar with a selection of wines by the glass and hundreds of bottles to choose from. Wooden decor, paper tablecloths and wines stored overhead. Good food too.

name: Fiddler’s Elbow
desc: The oldest Irish pub.

name: Il Margutta RistorArte
desc: A fairly decent vegetarian lunch buffet. The staff can point out the vegan eats. A decent value for the money. Near where Fellini once lived.

name: Fiaschetteria Beltramme da Cesaretto
hours: Open for lunch and dinner. Closed Sunday

desc: One of the best Cafe of the area. Try the homemade cremolato, probably one of the best in Rome.

name: Caffè Vaticano
desc: Delicious fruit gelato with exotic fruit bits, ice creams and coffees.

name: Osteria delle Commari
desc: An Italian restaurant that does not do pizza. A little expensive.

name: Siciliainbocca
desc: Nice Sicilian restaurant in the quiet (and somewhat boring) part of northern Prati. Try the swordfish and the lemon sorbet!

name: Babette caffe-ristorante

name: Pizzeria da Baffetto
desc: Old-fashioned, family feel pizzeria near Piazza Navona and the Pantheon, unarguably serving some of the best pizzas in Rome. Usually crowded but well-worth the occasional queuing.

name: Pasta In Corso
desc: There is another branch near the Pantheon, on Via della Maddalena, 43.

name: Alice
desc: Part of an Italian chain serving pizza al taglio (square pieces to be eaten by hand), dozens of pizzas to choose from.

name: Cul de Sac
hours: Kitchen works until 01:00. In Aug, closed for 2 we
desc: One of the best enoteche (wine bars) in Rome, serving a wide range of small dishes. The pate selection is a must-try. However, off-hours service is slow.

name: Il Bacaro
desc: You'd never know that you are three minutes walk from Piazza Navona and the Pantheon. Via degli Spagnoli is tiny, leafy and quiet. Il Bacaro seats about 24 inside and even fewer outside under the shade of an ancient vine

name: La Taverna del Ghetto
desc: Meat restaurant, excellent lamb dishes.

name: Tapa Loca
desc: Spanish food.

name: Taverna Lucifero

name: Forno di Campo de' Fiori

name: Frigidarium

name: Vineria Reggio
desc: Great place to sit for an affordable drink.

name: The Drunken Ship

name: Caffè Novecento
desc: Offers a very good variety of cakes, sweets, coffee and tea. The furnishing are nice, with couches as seats at some tables. Prices are mid-high range but worth every cent.

name: Caffè Giolitti
desc: An elegant coffee house in the style of the Belle Epoque, opened 1900. It offers among the best ice cream in Rome.

name: Ai Bozzi

name: Fior di luna
desc: Very good ice cream and made from fair trade products by an ice cream artist with a passion for taste.

name: Glass Hostaria
desc: Uber-modern trattoria.

name: Ivo a Trastevere
addr: Via di S. Francesco a Ripa 158
desc: Get here early if you want a table without a wait. Very popular pizzeria that attracts lengthy queues of young Romans, so it must be good.

name: La Gattabuia
desc: Serves pizza, pasta and steak. Great atmosphere and friendly staff. Unique location and décor.

name: Osteria dell'Aquila
desc: Mediterranean style restaurant. Menu is in Italian and English, and the waiters speak both languages. Open for lunch and dinner. The meals here are excellent and at very good prices. Make sure to try the seafood appetize

name: Osteria der Belli
desc: Run by four brothers from Sardinia. Particularly recommended for its seafood dishes.

name: Pizzeria La Boccaccia
addr: Via di San Francesco a Ripa 21

name: Il Vicola Da Tony

name: Trattoria de Gli Amici
desc: Very interesting place in the heart of Trastevere district. Run by very kind handicapped people, it has nice cuisine.

name: Vincenzo alla Lungaretta
desc: Out of the way. Great food and great service and a very reasonable price.

name: Vivi Bistrot
desc: Suitable for children as well. Useful for arranging a picnic in the park.

name: Enoteca Ferrara
desc: Luxury restaurant

name: Sora Lella
hours: closed Su, Tu morning and 2 weeks in August

name: Baccanale

name: Taverna Cestia

name: Da Bucatino
desc: Popular multi-roomed restaurant serving traditional Roman dishes.

name: Tutti Frutti
desc: Excellent Roman cooking at a good price. Menu in Italian and in English. Waiters speak English.

name: Volpetti

name: Ristorante Antico Forno
desc: Very nice for pizza and first courses.

name: Augustarello
desc: Good for typical Roman cuisine.

name: Checchino
desc: Excellent for typical Roman cuisine, with dishes owing much to the fact that Rome's abattoir used to be opposite.

name: Flavio al Velavevodetto
desc: Very good for typical Roman and other Italian cuisine.

name: Pizzeria da Remo
desc: One of the best for pizza.

name: Acqua e Farina
desc: Very good for pizza and a lot of particular recipes.

name: Il Grottino
desc: Good pizza place. Get there early at weekends.

name: Pizzeria Nuovo Mondo
desc: Very good for pizza.

name: L'Oasi della Birra

name: Old Bridge Gelateria
desc: Located across the street from the Vatican City wall if you're following it from San Pietro towards the Vatican Museum. Very cheap.

name: L'Insalata Ricca

name: Casetta di Campagna
hours: Closed on Monday. Sunday, Saturday and holidays al
desc: In the natural park Valle dei Casali they have very good meat. They also offer a fixed price menu for pizza (only for more than 4 people) which is good for a large gathering dinner. You need a car to reach the place.

name: La Pergola

name: Mama Che Pizza
desc: Worth stopping by if you're close to the EUR and it's cheap. They also own the deli right next to it, where you can also get miniature pizzas and breads.

name: Trattoria Zampagna
